source_text: Ἐπεὶ δ᾿ ἅπαξ γεγόναμεν ἐν τῷ περὶ τοῦ Πέτρου λόγῳ καὶ τῶν διδαξάντων τοὺς ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τὸν χριστιανισμὸν, οὐκ ἄτοπον ἡγοῦμαι παραθέσθαι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ τινα φωνὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ κατὰ Ἰωάννην εὐαγγελίου καὶ τὴν διήγησιν αὐτῆς. γέγραπται δὴ αὐτὸν εἰρηκέναι. „ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω λέγειν ὑμῖν, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι· ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν· οὐ γὰρ λαλήσει ἀφ᾿ ἑαυτοῦ, ἀλλ᾿ ὅσα ἀκούσει λαλήσει.“ καὶ ζητοῦμεν ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, τίνα ἦν τὰ „πολλὰ,“ ἃ εἶχε μὲν „λέγειν“ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἑαυτοῦ, οὐκ ἐδύναντο δὲ αὐτὰ „βαστάζειν“ τότε. καί φημι· μή ποθ᾿ ὡς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ συντραφεῖσι τῷ κατὰ τὸ γράμμα Μωϋσέως νόμῳ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις εἶχε μὲν „λέγειν,“ τίς ὁ ἀληθὴς νόμος, καὶ τίνων „ἐπουρανίων“ „ὑποδείγματι καὶ σκιᾷ“ ἡ παρὰ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις λατρεία ἐπετελεῖτο, καὶ τίνων „μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν“ „σκιὰν“ περιεῖχεν ὁ περὶ βρώσεως καὶ πόσεως καὶ ἑορτῶν καὶ νουμηνιῶν καὶ σαββάτων νόμος. καὶ „πολλὰ“ ἦν ταῦθ᾿, ἃ εἶχεν αὐτοῖς „λέγειν“· ὁρῶν δ᾿ ὅτι πάνυ χαλεπόν ἐστιν ἀπὸ ψυχῆς ἀνατρέπειν σχεδὸν συγγεννηθέντα καὶ συντραφέντα δόγματα μέχρι τῆς τοῦ ἀνδρὸς ἡλικίας καὶ πείσαντα τοὺς ἀνειληφότας αὐτὰ ὅτι ταῦτα μέν ἐστι θεῖα τὸ δὲ μετασαλεύειν αὐτά ἐστιν ἀσεβὲς, καὶ ἐν τῇ ὑπεροχῇ τῆς κατὰ Χριστὸν, τουτέστι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, „γνώσεως“ ἐλέγχειν αὐτὰ „σκύβαλα“ καὶ „ζημίαν,“ ὥστε πεισθῆναι τοὺς ἀκούοντας, ὑπερετίθετο εἰς ἐπιτηδειότερον καιρὸν τὸν μετὰ τὸ πάθος καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτοῦ. καὶ γὰρ ἀληθῶς ἦν ἀκαίρως προσαγόμενον τὸ βοήθημα τοῖς μηδέπω χωροῦσιν αὐτὸ, ἀνατρεπτικὸν τῆς περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὑπολήψεως τυγχάνον, ἣν ἤδη ἀνειλήφεσαν ὡς περὶ Χριστοῦ καὶ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος. καὶ πρόσχες εἰ μὴ νοῦν ἔχει οὐκ εὐκαταφρόνητον τὸ οὕτως ἀκοῦσαι τοῦ „ἔτι πολλὰ ἔχω ὑμῖν λέγειν, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ δύνασθε βαστάζειν ἄρτι“· „πολλὰ“ γὰρ τὰ τῆς τοῦ νόμου κατὰ τὰ πνευματικὰ διηγήσεως καὶ σαφηνείας· καὶ οὐκ ἐδύναντό πως „βαστάζειν“ αὐτὰ οἱ μαθηταὶ, ἐν Ἰουδαίοις γεγεννημένοι καὶ ἀνατεθραμμένοι τότε. οἶμαι δ᾿ ὅτι καὶ ἐπεὶ τύπος μὲν ἦν ἐκεῖνα, ἀλήθεια δὲ ἃ ἔμελλε διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, διὰ τοῦτο λέλεκται· „ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὁδηγήσει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν“· ὡς εἰ ἔλεγεν· εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τῶν πραγμάτων. ὧν ἐν τοῖς τύποις γενόμενοι ᾤεσθε τὴν ἀληθῆ λατρείαν λατρεύειν τῷ θεῷ. καὶ κατὰ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἦλθε „τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας“ ἐπὶ τὸν Πέτρον, λέγον πρὸς αὐτὸν περὶ τῶν τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν τῆς γῆς καὶ πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· „ἀναστὰς, Πέτρε. θῦσον καὶ φάγε.“ καὶ ἦλθε πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔτι δεισιδαιμονοῦντα, φησὶ γὰρ καὶ πρὸς τὴν θείαν φωνήν· „μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέ ποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.“ καὶ ἐδίδαξε τὸν περὶ βρωμάτων ἀληθῶν καὶ πνευματικῶν λόγον ἐν τῷ „ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισε σὺ μὴ κοίνου.“ καὶ ἑξῆς ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὀπτασίᾳ „τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας“ ὁδηγοῦν „εἰς τὴν ἀλήθειαν πᾶσαν“ τὸν Πέτρον τὰ πολλὰ ἔλεγεν αὐτῷ, ἃ οὐκ ἐδύνατο „βαστάζειν,“ ὅτε κατὰ σάρκα αὐτῷ ἔτι ὁ Ἰησοῦς συνῆν. ἀλλὰ περὶ μὲν τούτων ἄλλος ἔσται καιρὸς πρὸς τὸ διηγήσασθαι περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὴν ἐκδοχὴν τοῦ Μωϋσέως νόμου.
pass_a_gloss: Since once we have come to the account (λόγος) about Peter and those who taught (διδάσκω) Christianity (χριστιανισμός) to those in the circumcision (περιτομή), I think it not out of place (ἄτοπος) to set beside (παρατίθημι) a certain utterance (φωνή) of Jesus from the Gospel according to John and its exposition (διήγησις). Written that he said: [John 16:12–13] yet many things I have to say to you, but you cannot bear (βαστάζω) now; when that one comes, the Spirit of truth (ἀλήθεια), he will guide (ὁδηγέω) you into all the truth; for he will not speak from himself, but as many things as he hears he will speak. We seek (ζητέω) in the place (τόπος) what were the many things which Jesus had to say to his disciples but they could not bear then. And I say: perhaps (μή ποτε), to the apostles as Jews and brought up together (συντρέφω) with the law of Moses according to the letter (γράμμα), he had to say what is the true law, and of what heavenly things (ἐπουράνια) as copy (ὑπόδειγμα) and shadow (σκιά) the worship (λατρεία) among Jews was performed, and of what coming goods (μέλλοντα ἀγαθά) the law about food (βρῶσις), drink (πόσις), feasts (ἑορταί), new moons (νουμηνίαι), sabbaths (σάββατα) contained a shadow. And these were the many things he had to say; but seeing that it is very hard (χαλεπός) to overturn (ἀνατρέπω) from a soul doctrines (δόγματα) almost born-with (συγγεννάω) and brought-up-with up to man’s age, and having persuaded those who took them up that these are divine (θεῖος) and to unsettle (μετασαλεύω) them is impious (ἀσεβής), and in the surpassingness (ὑπεροχή) of the knowledge (γνῶσις) according to Christ, that is the truth, to refute (ἐλέγχω) them as refuse (σκύβαλα) and loss (ζημία), so as the hearers be persuaded, he postponed (ὑπερτίθημι) to a more suitable time (καιρός), the one after his passion (πάθος) and resurrection (ἀνάστασις). For truly the help (βοήθημα) would be brought unseasonably (ἀκαίρως) to those not yet containing (χωρέω) it, being subversive of the conception (ὑπόληψις) about Jesus which they had already taken up, as about Christ and Son of the living God. Consider whether it has a sense (νοῦς) not easily despised (εὐκαταφρόνητος) so to hear the ‘yet many things…’: for many are the matters of the exposition and clarification (σαφήνεια) of the law according to the spiritual things (τὰ πνευματικά); and the disciples could not somehow bear them, born and reared among Jews then. I think also, since those things were a type (τύπος), and truth what the Holy Spirit was going to teach, for this reason it was said ‘when that one comes…’, as if he said: into all the truth of the things (πράγματα), in whose types being, you thought you were worshipping the true worship to God. And according to the promise (ἐπαγγελία) of Jesus the Spirit of truth came upon Peter, saying about quadrupeds, creeping things, birds: rise, Peter, kill (θύω) and eat; and came to him still being superstitious (δεισιδαιμονέω), for he says even to the divine voice: by no means, Lord… And taught the doctrine about true and spiritual foods (βρώματα) in ‘what God cleansed do not make common’. And after that vision the Spirit of truth, guiding Peter into all truth, told him the many things which he could not bear when Jesus was still with him according to the flesh. But about these there will be another occasion to expound the matters of the interpretation (ἐκδοχή) of the law of Moses.
pass_b_english: Since we have now come to speak of Peter and of those who taught Christianity to the people of the circumcision, I think it not out of place to set down a saying of Jesus from the Gospel according to John, with its interpretation. It is written that he said: “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak on his own, but whatever he hears he will speak” (John 16:12–13).

And we ask in this passage what the “many things” were that Jesus had “to say” to his disciples, but which they could not then “bear.” And I say: perhaps, since the apostles were Jews and had been brought up in the law of Moses according to the letter, he had “to say” to them what the true law is, and of what “heavenly things” the worship among the Jews was carried out “as a copy and shadow” (Hebrews 8:5), and of what “good things to come” the law about eating and drinking, festivals, new moons and sabbaths contained “a shadow” (Hebrews 10:1; Colossians 2:16–17). And these were the “many things” that he had “to say” to them.

But he saw that it is very hard to uproot from the soul doctrines that have been almost born with a man and brought up with him to the age of manhood, and that have persuaded those who received them that they are divine and that to unsettle them is impious; and very hard to prove them, by the surpassing worth of the “knowledge” that accords with Christ, that is, with the truth, to be “refuse” and “loss” (Philippians 3:7–8), so that the hearers would be persuaded. So he put it off to a more suitable time, the time after his passion and resurrection. For truly the help would have been offered out of season to those not yet able to receive it, since it would have overturned the conception of Jesus they had already received, that he was the Christ and the Son of the living God (Matthew 16:16).

And consider whether understanding the words “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now” in this way does not yield a meaning that is far from contemptible. For the “many things” are those that belong to the interpretation and clarification of the law in its spiritual sense; and at that time the disciples, born and brought up among the Jews, were somehow unable to “bear” them.

I think too that, because those things were a type, while what the Holy Spirit was going to teach them was the truth, it was for this reason said: “When he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth” (John 16:13), as if he were saying: into all the truth of the realities, while you, being occupied with their types, supposed that you were offering God the true worship.

And according to the promise of Jesus, “the Spirit of truth” came upon Peter, saying to him about the four-footed creatures and creeping things of the earth and the birds of the sky: “Rise, Peter, kill and eat” (Acts 10:13). And the Spirit came to him while he was still superstitious; for even to the divine voice he says: “By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common and unclean” (Acts 10:14). And he taught the doctrine of true and spiritual foods in the words “What God has cleansed, you must not call common” (Acts 10:15). And after that vision “the Spirit of truth,” guiding Peter “into all the truth,” told him the many things that he could not “bear” while Jesus was still with him in the flesh. But there will be another occasion for explaining these matters, which concern the interpretation of the law of Moses.

choices.why: ‘κατὰ Χριστόν, τουτέστι τὴν ἀλήθειαν’ now ‘accords with Christ, that is, with the truth’

choices.term: not … should not be lightly dismissed
choices.why: double negative ‘not … should not be lightly dismissed’ recast as ‘far from contemptible’ (litotes kept)
‘τότε’ placed with the inability to bear; ‘πως’ kept as ‘somehow’
subject made explicit: ‘the Spirit came to him’ (neuter πνεῦμα; was an ambiguous ‘he’)

translator_notes: Copy-text: staged source_2.json section 2 (Koetschau 2.2); row complete. John 16:12–13 is quoted twice; the second time Origen transposes ‘ὑμῖν λέγειν’, which does not change the sense. The phrases ‘heavenly things’, ‘copy and shadow’ (Hebrews 8:5), ‘shadow of good things to come’ (Hebrews 10:1) and the list ‘eating, drinking, festivals, new moons, sabbaths’ (Colossians 2:16–17) are woven together; all cited inline. ‘ἐν τῇ ὑπεροχῇ τῆς κατὰ Χριστόν, τουτέστι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, γνώσεως’ draws on Philippians 3:7–8 (τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ … σκύβαλα … ζημίαν); the gloss ‘that is, the truth’ identifies Christ with the truth and may echo John 14:6 (possible allusion, not cited inline). The infinitive ἐλέγχειν is taken as a second object of ‘it is very hard’, parallel to ἀνατρέπειν. ‘Christ and Son of the living God’ echoes Peter’s confession (Matthew 16:16). ‘ᾤεσθε τὴν ἀληθῆ λατρείαν λατρεύειν τῷ θεῷ’: Origen shifts to the second person plural within the paraphrase of Jesus’s words; kept as ‘you … supposed’. ‘True worship’ may echo John 4:23 (possible only). ‘δεισιδαιμονοῦντα’ rendered ‘superstitious’ (scrupulous about the food laws); Origen’s own word, not softened. ‘πνεῦμα’ capitalised as Spirit where it is the Spirit of truth / Holy Spirit; ‘law in its spiritual sense’ (κατὰ τὰ πνευματικά) lower case. No LXX renumbering arises in this chapter.
